title: RX: a zero-gap 1-byte runt after a dropped frame is not counted
body:
[R1]

Found by the cleared-context review of PR #24 and measured at both `9d5fb025` and PR #24's head `facb559f`; PRE-EXISTING, so it was filed rather than folded into that PR.

## What is wrong

A drop is lost when a 1-byte runt arrives in the cycle immediately after a dropped frame's end of frame. Two increments of `drop_cnt_r` live in the same `always_ff`: the deferred-finalize arm at `hdl/wire/KL_gptp_rx_parser.sv:292` (`drop_cnt_r <= drop_cnt_r + 16'd1;`) and the one-byte-frame arm at `:456` (the identical statement). `fin_r` is asserted for the cycle after eof, and a zero-gap 1-byte frame asserts `rx_sof_i && rx_eof_i` in exactly that cycle, so both non-blocking assignments target `drop_cnt_r` on one edge and only one increment lands.

## Measured

With a directed probe appended to the parser testbench (RTL unmodified, `git diff -- hdl/` empty):

- at `facb559f`, an unlisted-type frame followed with no gap by a 1-byte runt: `FAIL P3 unlisted then zero-gap runt: two drops got 002f exp 0030`; with one idle cycle between them, `PASS P3b unlisted then 1-gap runt: two drops`.
- at base `9d5fb025`, the same collision using a foreign-domain Sync in place of the unlisted frame (the base has no unlisted-type drop): `FAIL BASEPROBE zero-gap runt after drop got 001c exp 001d`; `PASS BASEPROBE 1-gap runt after drop`.

Everything else tested for "counted exactly once" holds: nine unlisted frames delivered back to back give nine drops with no event and no bank write; an unlisted frame followed with no gap by a good Sync gives one drop and a clean `w0` with event code 1; truncation before the type byte (10 octets) and at the type byte (15 octets) each give one drop and no bank write; a mid-frame reset clears `drop_cnt_o` and the next Sync dispatches.

## Impact

No effect on the parent campaign today: its only runt negative is a 6-byte frame sent standalone, and its nine unknown-type probes are 68-byte frames. On a real fabric FIFO, a zero-gap 1-byte runt after any drop under-counts by one, and `dbg_rx_drop_o` is the oracle the parent's conformance probes read, so a silently missed drop weakens every probe that asserts a counted refusal.

## Acceptance

- [ ] The two increment paths cannot collide: the counter advances once per refused frame regardless of the inter-frame gap, including a 1-byte runt in the cycle after a dropped frame's eof.
- [ ] A parser test covers the zero-gap case for both orderings (drop then runt, runt then drop) and a planted mutation restoring the collision goes red; README counts updated.
- [ ] No change to the accepted-frame path: a good frame following a dropped one with no gap still dispatches with a clean bank word.

The engine README already contemplates the neighbouring shape (row 30, "a zero-gap 1-byte runt cannot poison the predecessor's stamp"); the drop-count face of it is the uncovered corner.
